    AI Overview
    Artemis 1 launched on November 16, 2022, at 1:47 a.m. EST from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The uncrewed test flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft lasted 25.5 days, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean on December 11, 2022. 
    You can watch a replay of the Artemis 1 launch:
    56s
    VideoFromSpace
    YouTube• Nov 16, 2023
    Key Details of the Mission: 
    • Purpose: An uncrewed flight test to verify the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft systems before crewed missions.
    • Launch Vehicle:
      Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1.
    • Duration: 25 days, 10 hours, 53 minutes.
    • Key Milestone: The Orion spacecraft performed two lunar flybys and traveled nearly 270,000 miles from Earth.
    • Splashdown: December 11, 2022. 
    The mission was the first in the Artemis program aimed at returning humans to the Moon.

    People also ask
    Why did Artemis 1 fail?
    Some problems occurred during testing and rehearsal, but the first real “failure to launch” happened on August 29, 2022, when one of the four rocket engines overheated and other issues led to a launch cancellation. NASA attempted again in early September 2022, but a fuel leak in a supply hose caused another scrub.

    Did Artemis 2 happen yet?
    NASA has successfully launched Artemis 2, its first astronaut mission to the moon since 1972. Liftoff took place on April 1, sending four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon aboard the Orion spacecraft. The actually moon flyby is today, Monday, April 6. Splashdown will be on Friday, April 10.2 days ago
